column2: Pick one of the epochs you have passed: the look, goods and music change. Under each name: the current epoch shows your balance, as in the counter; passed epochs show what was earned in them. New coins, including offline ones, count in the selected epoch. New epochs unlock with time travel.
Changes the trees, weather and mood of the street. "Auto" uses the date on your device.
Phew, the heat. Water, and plenty of it.
Just catching my breath, then back to work. One minute. Two.
The sun burns like the tax office: no escape.
Cold water is the best reward. Well, besides money.
Shade and a glass of water. Now that's life.
{0} is in town. Tap to catch: each gives coins, and both together give a crystal.
Too slow. Be faster next time.
Ghosts in town. Tap them: each gives coins, and catching them all gives a crystal.
Caught: {0} of {1}. Catch them all for a crystal.
The ghosts melted away. Be faster next time.
Collected for the drum: {0}. {1} buy an extra spin of the wheel.
✉️ The mail truck arrived. Pick up the letter by the road.
Hi, boss. Found an extra penny in the till and thought of you right away. Don't ask whose it is. Here's a bonus from the post office.
It's Zoya. I came up with a promo: whoever reads this letter gets a bonus. That's you. Don't thank me, just recommend me.
Bodie. Built a mailbox and sent the first letter. The bonus is attached like a nail to a plank: firmly and without extra words.
Hoo. I did the math: you deserve a bonus. The books balance, no need to check. You'll check anyway.
The plan: you read this letter, get a bonus, we all come out ahead. Deal? I'll take silence as agreement.
It's Pao. The letter has bamboo and luck. The discounts are gone, but the bonus is real.
The circus is on its way to you!
Night one. Something quietly ticks in Capy's pocket. Not a call from the bank.
Night two. The ticking is louder. Definitely not an alarm clock this time.
Sit down. How was your day? Mine was prickly, as usual.
So, how was it? Profit's fine, mood's questionable.
Sit. How's your day? Mine's like a dam: it holds, but something's cracking.
Plank on plank. Tell me what's up. No renovation plans, please.
Sit down. How's your day? I sold two things that don't exist.
Tell me the news. I've already come up with three promos and one excuse.
Take your time. How's your day? I let no one through. Boring and wonderful.
Sit. Slow is beautiful. Especially when nobody is in a hurry.
Hey, friend. How's your day? Heavy, but with lunch.
Sit. Want a sandwich? I don't ask twice.
Hoo, sit down. How's your day? My books balanced. Scary and nice.
Tell me the news. I'll write it down. No, not for the tax office.
Quack. How's your day? Mine's clean. Yours?
Sit, rest your feet. Then tell me who tracked in the dirt today.
Ribbit. How's your day? Mine was stylish. Yours, we'll fix.
Sit, let's talk. About trends, about people, about people's trends.
Quick version: how's your day? Mine's on plan. The plan is classified.
Sit, I have an idea. First you tell me about your day, then comes my slide.
Hi. How's your day? Mine's like bamboo: sturdy and not always tasty.
Sit, share the news. No spoilers though: I have my own content.
Purr. How's your day? I was charging in the sun. Healthier than working.
Sit, I'll listen. Just stay quiet when I reach for the wire.
Sit. I forget nothing, so tell me about your day carefully.
An elephant's life is long. How's your day? No fiction, please.
Time of day (the sun and moon move on their own, a day takes 5 minutes):
The coins in my quills are frosted. Counting is cold and ringing now.
Zoya tied a scarf onto one of my quills. The rest will have to cope.
In winter only the part of the till under my paw stays warm.
Planks sing in the frost. Nobody asked, yet it sounds like an orchestra.
Mikhas brought crates and they smell of snow. I'll put them by the stove to wake up.
I dream of a workshop with a fireplace. The plans exist, on a tea napkin.
Frost draws patterns on the window. That's competition, and it's pretty.
My ears are frozen but my mood is pink. A hat would help, a pink one.
Zhuzha says a scarf is an accessory. I say it's a rescue, just a pretty one.
I'm slow and the cold is even slower. At last, someone to race.
It's warm in the shell. The others have pockets; let them envy me.
This shop has seen a hundred and forty winters. This one feels colder. Or I'm older.
I'm a bear, I'm not cold. I just want to sleep until spring.
The crates froze into a tower. Spike says "architecture". I say "problem".
